quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jason Nalbandian on why RPO grows faster than revenue: EMCOR had 'significant bookings in Q1 and Q2' and carries more revenue in RPO than historically. It used to start a year needing to book and earn 60% of that year's revenue in that year; that share has steadily come down as project sizes rose and pipelines expanded, to about 40%-45% in recent years, which drives the disconnect between RPO growth and revenue growth. CEO Tony Guzzi (his turns are labelled 'Moderator' in the saved transcript), with the CFO: RPO follows the accounting definition - an executed contract with a firm price, or an approved change order - and never includes expected follow-on buildings on a campus, so EMCOR is 'on the conservative side with RPOs'.
quarterly_data.figure: share of a year's revenue still to book and earn in-year: 60% historically, about 40%-45% in recent years
